newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba Pool, Pioneer in venture at Roblin.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba Pool, Pioneer in venture at Roblin.

text.p: Two of Canada's top six grain handling firms entered a joint venture to build a high through put terminal and farm service center in northwest Manitoba, a joint statement said.

Manitoba Pool Elevators and Pioneer Grain Co Ltd plan to build a 12,000-tonne grain terminal just outside Roblin, Manitoba, along a Canadian National Railway Co line, about 15 km from the Saskatchewan border.
The firms will begin construction of the 12,000 tonne facility next spring. It is scheduled to open next fall.
That region produces wheat, barley, canola and flax.
"We are business competitors but this joint venture just makes good business sense," MPE president Charlie Swanson said in the statement.

Manitoba Pool is a privately-held cooperative owned by 16,000 Manitoba farmers. It handled 2.8 million tonnes of grains and oilseeds in crop year 1994/95 (Aug/July) with net earnings before taxes of C$7.7 million. It held 53 percent of the Manitoba market.
"Our corporate structures are different but the objectives of both businesses are the same," Pioneer president Curt Vossen said in the statement.

Pioneer Grain is a family-owned grain firm that posted sales of more than C$1.0 billion in fiscal 1995 (Jan/Dec), had 970 employees and operated 139 elevators across the Prairies. Net earnings were not disclosed.

The joint venture between the companies parallels another such deal announced December 22, 1995 between Saskatchewan Wheat Pool and Cargill Ltd to build a high through put export terminal on Canada's West Coast.
Cargill Ltd is a unit of U.S.-owned Cargill Inc.

The Cargill/SWP deal surprised many industry participants who contended that family firms were more likely to enter into such agreements with each other while Canada's three cooperatives would work together on such projects.
